I18nDemo.title: Simple locale switching with preserved client state
I18nDemo.description: This page uses a cookie-backed locale. Switching language refreshes the current route so the translated copy updates, while the local counter and draft note stay alive.
I18nDemo.serverRefreshedNote: If this timestamp changes after switching language, the server really re-rendered.
I18nDemo.switcherDescription: These buttons update a locale cookie through a server action, then call router.refresh() on the current page.
I18nDemo.persistenceTitle: Client state that should survive the locale change
I18nDemo.draftPlaceholder: Type something here, then switch language
I18nDemo.mountedHint: If this time stays the same, the component was preserved instead of remounted.
I18nDemo.persistenceHint: The counter, timestamp and note are plain React useState values, not localStorage.
I18nDemo.noteBody: Cookie-based locale switching is the easiest way to keep state during language changes. If you later move to /en and /ms routes, that route change can remount parts of the tree, so you would usually persist state in the URL, a cookie, localStorage, or a provider above the locale segment.
